answer: Make every identity hold its own sealed archive: about 200 GB encoded with that agent's key, a slow sealing pass that takes hours, so two accounts can't share one copy. At random moments a verifier asks for a few blocks plus a proof that must arrive within 5 seconds, far too fast to re-seal from a shared master. Disk runs roughly $2 per identity a month (illustrative), so a nebula of 1,000 fakes rents 200 TB, about $2,000 monthly, linear in clones. Each epoch adds a layer like shale; an ocean of keys with no disk behind them fails the first audit.
